proof_0025.moves: Two pre-0-hypercovers that are isomorphic generate the same sieve. Prove the two sieves are equal by antisymmetry of the order on sieves: apply the already-proved monotonicity lemma (a morphism of pre-0-hypercovers gives an inclusion of generated sieves) once to the forward map of the isomorphism and once to its inverse.

proof_0026.moves: Exhibit a witness: if a simplicial set is nonempty (so its set of 0-simplices is inhabited), pick an arbitrary 0-simplex with choice and package it as a simplex of dimension 0 to build the Nonempty instance. The whole content is producing that one element.

proof_0027.moves: For an isomorphism of cones, the underlying maps compose to the identity. The only real step is that composition and identity in the category of cones are computed on the underlying morphisms, after which the statement is just the inverse-hom identity of an isomorphism in a category; the rest is simp's rewriting residue.

proof_0028.moves: Over a subsingleton coefficient ring the quaternions are a subsingleton. The proof just reuses the instance for the general quaternion algebra, since the Hamilton quaternions are by definition the algebra with parameters (-1,0,-1); the substantive fact (a quaternion algebra over a subsingleton ring is a subsingleton, via the equivalence with 4-tuples) sits inside an anonymous auto-generated lemma.

proof_0029.moves: Purely definitional: the modulo operation on UInt8 is defined by transporting Fin's modulo through the underlying Fin value, so both sides of the equation reduce to the same term and rfl closes it. No mathematical idea is involved beyond unfolding the instance.

proof_0030.moves: Given a divides b, show a * (b / a) = b. Commute the product to put it in the form (b / a) * a and then apply the cancellation lemma for division followed by multiplication. Two steps: a commutativity rewrite plus the divisibility cancellation fact.

proof_0031.moves: The arrow of an object obtained by lifting a functor to monomorphisms-over is the hom of the image object. True by definition: lifting into the full subcategory of monos changes nothing about the underlying over-category object, so both sides are the same projection and rfl closes it.

proof_0032.moves: Adding a fixed natural number on the left of a Fin index is injective, so natAdd m i = natAdd m j iff i = j. The content is: natAdd is strictly monotone, strict monotonicity gives injectivity, and injectivity upgrades to an iff on equations.

proof_0033.moves: Composing two induced graph isomorphisms on subsets equals the isomorphism induced by the composite. This is definitional: both sides carry the same underlying function on the subtype and the same adjacency proof, so rfl works. No idea beyond unfolding induce and comp.

proof_0034.moves: A simps-generated component lemma: the inverse of the natural isomorphism comparing a reindexed pointwise product with the original is, at each object, the stated comparison map. The isomorphism is built by ofComponents and then symm'd, so its inverse component is definitionally the given map and the proof is reflexivity.

proof_0035.moves: Relabelling the empty CNF gives the empty CNF. Unfold relabel as a map over the clause array and empty as the array coming from the empty list; then mapping over the empty list is empty, transported across the list-to-array coercion. Everything else is simp's rewriting residue.

proof_0036.moves: If a composite factors as f1 followed by f2 and the composite is locally surjective, then f2 is locally surjective. The proof substitutes the factorization equation to replace f3 by f1 followed by f2, then invokes the already-proved statement for an actual composite. The only genuine move is the substitution plus the citation.

proof_0037.moves: For ideals, J*I sup I = I. Since the product of two ideals is contained in the right factor, I is the larger of the two, and the characterization of when a supremum equals its right argument (namely when the left is below it) converts that containment into the equality.

proof_0038.moves: Scaling a set by a group element commutes with intersection. Since the scalar action of a group element is a bijection, in particular injective, and the scaled set is by definition the image of the set under that map, the general fact that images of injective maps preserve intersections finishes it.

proof_0039.moves: A transfer lemma: the extensional hash map is a thin wrapper around the dependent extensional hash map, so unwrap to the inner structure and apply the corresponding dependent-map lemma verbatim. No independent mathematical content.

proof_0040.moves: A list has length n+1 exactly when it is a cons of a head onto a tail of length n. The real argument is a case split on the list: nil gives a contradiction on lengths, cons exhibits the head and tail as the witnesses. Here that argument is discharged wholesale by automation and lives inside an anonymous private lemma, so no citation names the idea.

proof_0041.moves: In degree zero, the map from paths to simplices produced by strict Segal-ness is just the single vertex of the path. This holds by construction of spineToSimplex at the base case, so the proof is reflexivity; the content is the unfolding of that definition.

proof_0042.moves: Rewriting only: the conjunction that x is weakly between y and z and that z is weakly between x and y is equivalent to x = y. Use the symmetry of weak betweenness to reverse one of the triples, then the already-proved swap-right criterion, then flip the resulting equality with symmetry of equality.

proof_0043.moves: Continuity at a point of the pointwise infimum of two functions. The bundled lattice-operation version of the same statement is definitionally the pointwise one, so the proof is a one-line restatement of the primed lemma with no new content.

proof_0044.moves: Transfer lemma: reading an element of a mapped raw hash map. Unwrap the non-dependent raw map to its dependent inner representation, extract the underlying well-formedness witness from the wrapper, and apply the corresponding dependent constant-type lemma.

proof_0045.moves: The zeroth component of the comparison natural transformation between two composable-arrow diagrams is the identity. The transformation is built componentwise from identity, identity and the third map, so the zeroth component is the identity by construction and rfl closes it.

proof_0046.moves: Monadic flatMap over an array of subtype elements stripped of their proofs equals the flatMap of the composed function. Rewrite the unattached array as a map of the subtype projection using the subtype form of flatMapM, then adjust the function under the binder with the congruence lemma for flatMapM. The remaining terms are binder-name hints, well-founded recursion markers and simp residue.

proof_0047.moves: Mapping the identity over a raw dependent hash map yields an equivalent map. Bridge the raw-level map to the internal well-sized (Raw-zero) map using the map-equation lemma, which requires producing the positivity of the bucket array size from the well-formedness hypothesis to build the subtype witness, and then apply the internal statement that mapping the identity gives an equivalent map.

proof_0048.moves: Removing entry i after entry j from a dependent tuple agrees, up to heterogeneous equality, with removing them in the other order using predAbove and succAbove to relabel the indices. Reduce the heterogeneous equality of dependent functions to a pointwise statement, introduce the index by a substitution, unfold removeNth as precomposition with succAbove, and then the whole thing rests on the index identity relating succAbove applied three times to predAbove.
